title: LLM Adapter + Edge Accelerator Lab: step-by-step workshop and samples
summary: Hands-on lab that walks solutions engineers and customer engineers through building an lightweight adapter for running Redwood inference on edge-attached accelerators. Focus on latency-aware batching, graceful fallback to hosted variants, KV-cache prefetch strategies, and a small local emulator for testing. Designed for a 90–120 minute workshop with hands-on exercises.
objectives: 1) Build and run a minimal adapter process that talks to a Redwood-compatible runtime (local emulator provided). 2) Implement batching & backoff logic to meet 99th percentile latency targets. 3) Add a simple KV-cache prefetch hook to reduce repeated prefix cost. 4) Capture metrics and run a cost/latency profile. 5) Produce a short proposal template for customer POC next steps.
audience_and_prereqs: Intended audience: solutions engineers, customer infra engineers, and platform PMs. Prereqs: basic familiarity with HTTP/gRPC, Python or Go, Docker, and a laptop with Docker + 8GB RAM; recommended: an instance with a small GPU for full accelerator path testing (NVIDIA T4 / A10). Knowledge of Redwood API concepts (models, rollouts, fallback) is helpful.
materials_to_prepare:
- Clone repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/edge-adapter-samples.git
- Docker installed and running
- (Optional) GPU instance or cloud VM with drivers for accelerator testing
- Local emulator binary (packaged in repo)
- Sample prompt sets and short eval harness (included)
lab_setup_instructions:
1) git clone the repo and cd into /labs/edge-adapter. 2) ./tools/setup_emulator.sh to spin up a lightweight local server that mimics Redwood endpoints (text generation + kv-prefetch hook). 3) Start the adapter scaffold: python3 adapter/scaffold.py --config labs/example-config.yaml (or go run ./adapter/main.go --local). 4) Confirm connectivity: curl http://localhost:8080/health returns ok. 5) Start the load generator: ./tools/load_runner --profile quick-qa.
Notes: the emulator supports artificial delay injection to exercise backoff/fallback logic. Config file explains model variants for fallback (e.g., "gpt-small-quant" vs "gpt-medium-fp16").
workshop_flow: Part A (~20m): walkthrough of architecture (adapter, runtime, KV-cache, fallback). Part B (~40m): implement a batching policy and observe latency at different QPS. Part C (~20m): add KV-prefetch for recurring prefixes and measure token delta. Part D (~20m): create a short customer POC doc with acceptance criteria and rollout plan.
tasks_and_exercises:
Exercise 1 — Minimal adapter: wire up the scaffold to call emulator generation endpoint and return a JSON response; verify basic correctness.
Exercise 2 — Batching/backoff: implement a size- and time-based batcher (max_batch=8, max_delay_ms=45). Simulate slow backend and implement exponential backoff that reduces batch size when 95th p99 latency exceeds SLO. Test by toggling emulator delay.
Exercise 3 — KV-prefetch hook: implement a prefetch pass that looks up recent prefixes stored in a lightweight LRU cache. Add a telemetry counter for cache hits/misses. Use provided sample conversation set to exercise prefetch.
Exercise 4 — Fallback policy: configure adapter to route to a cheaper quantized variant when GPU pool is saturated; simulate saturation via emulator and validate successful fallbacks with intact responses.
Deliverable: each pair should produce a short PR that adds one unit test and an instrumentation point (span or metric) for their change.
metrics_to_capture_and_dashboards: Capture: request_count, batch_size_histogram, p50/p95/p99 latency, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, fallback_count, backend_error_rate, cost_estimate_tokens. Suggested dashboard panels: latency heatmap by model_variant, batch size over time, cache hit rate, fallback triggers. We provide a Grafana JSON under repo/tools/grafana/edge-lab-dashboard.json (linked artifact).
acceptance_criteria_for_customer_poc: - 99th percentile latency <= 350ms for target prompt set at pilot QPS (document QPS). - Cache hits reduce per-request token generation tokens by at least 20% on recurring queries. - Fallback policy triggers without user-visible errors and keeps request success rate >= 99.5%. - Clear rollout plan: staged canary on 5% traffic -> 25% -> full. - Short cost estimate comparing hosted vs edge-assisted per-1M requests.
postlab_exercises_and_extension_ideas: 1) Add model quantization selection logic based on recent output-quality regression tests. 2) Integrate HSM-based key access for private deployments in the adapter. 3) Swap the local emulator for a real Redwood Dedicated endpoint and re-run the profile. 4) Build an automated A/B test harness that measures user-perceived quality difference between variants.
troubleshooting_notes:
Symptom: p99 spikes when batch size rises. Check: backend queuing, kernel stalls, inappropriate max_delay. Mitigation: reduce max_batch, enable eager fallback, add token-based early termination heuristics.
Symptom: cache not being used. Check: prefix normalization mismatches, eviction policy too small, missing instrumentation.
Symptom: adapter crash under load. Check heap/GC (if Go, goroutine leaks), connection pool exhaustion, and proper backpressure on client sockets. Increase file descriptor ulimit for heavy load tests.
customer_poc_template_snippet:
POC name: Edge Adapter latency pilot
Goal: Demonstrate 3x improvement in median cost-per-inference while keeping p99 latency within target.
Scope: 2 weeks, integrate adapter with customer staging cluster, run 100k requests with production-like prompts.
Acceptance: metrics in Acceptance Criteria section above.
Risks & mitigations: GPU driver mismatch -> use emulator first; data locality issues -> run small on-prem smoke tests; security -> use KMS + mTLS between adapter and runtime.
Next steps: schedule deep-dive with infra team, propose Dedicated capacity pricing for pilot.
notes_and_references: - See repo samples under /adapter and /tools for scripts. - Related ticket: PROJ-1324 (edge adapter quickstart). - Helpful reading: internal doc 'serving-runtime-batching-patterns' and 'kv-cache-patterns'. - Slack thread: #solutions-edge-pocs for active Q&A.
final_comments: This lab is intentionally lightweight so customer engineers can complete the end-to-end flow in a single session. Encourage pairs to open PRs for their changes and to capture lessons learned in the PR description. Use provided metrics to write a short 1-page summary for the customer after the session.
expected_artifacts_from_lab:
- small adapter PR with unit test and metric
- short profiling report (CSV) showing p50/p95/p99 for baseline and after caching
- one-page customer POC proposal
- screenshots of dashboard panels or exported grafana JSON
